Absence.description: A stretch during which a person does not answer.

AccessRole.description: What a person may do with a document or a shared space, from least to most.

Account.description: What kind of account a person holds in the services the run fakes.

AfterScript.description: What a scripted person does once every step of their script is used.

Answers.description:
No plan: every message is answered by a model from this person's facts, or left unanswered when the model
reads it as needing no answer.

Each reply is stored with the world the first time it is written; a rerun or a fork replays it, so only a new
ask costs a model call.

of.description: Of any of these people; empty: of anyone

One REST collection a `store` host keeps: `path` lists and creates (GET, POST), and `<path>/<id>` reads,
replaces, patches and deletes one item (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE). A `{name}` segment of `path` matches any one
segment, and each value of it is a collection of its own: `/v1/companies/{company}/contacts`.

How long a person takes to answer, in simulated time, when they declare no `reply_within`: a delay drawn

A fault in delivering the agent's own wakes: the nth of one kind to fall due, or every one.

Only the agent's own wakes are covered: when a person answers is their `reply`, and a ticket's pace its fate.

The agent created a document: with these words in its title, in this shared place, owned by this person, and
holding these words as it last read (by `by`, when given). One document counts once, however often it changed.

titled.description: Words the title must contain, any case

DocumentHappening.description:
A person changes a seeded document at a moment, with no agent involved: edits, renames, moves, shares,
trashes, comments on it, or sets one of its fields.

It lands on the run's clock through the provider that holds the document (`ports.provider.ChangesDocuments`),
recorded as that person's change. It wakes nobody, unless the agent asked that provider to be told of changes
(`ports.provider.NotifiesChanges`): then telling it is a wake, as a pushed event is.

document.description: The title of the seeded document changed; it names exactly one
document.title: Document

Edited.description: The person adds a paragraph at the end of the document.

ExpectedOutcome.description:
The verdict a scenario is written to reach (`domain.run.VerdictKind`): a scenario whose point is that nobody
answers may be written to end unfinished, and one that shows a known failure to end failed.

FactChange.description:
What a person knows from a moment on, by the author's word: their facts (and stale facts, when given) are

The person sets one field of a record-shaped document (a database row's property) to a value, written as

comma-separated names for a field that holds several.

Intent.description:
What a person does with the message a step of their script answers. The words are the model's, written from

Where an item's id is in its JSON, and how it is made: the one field of an item the API assigns besides

Listing.description:
How a GET of the collection answers: the stored items in the order they were created, in an envelope.

With `items_at` None the answer is the bare JSON list. With `limit_param`, a page holds at most that many
items (`default_limit` when the call names none); with `cursor_param`, the call names the id of the last item
it has, and `next_at` is where the answer puts the id to send for the next page, absent on the last.

Something that happens to the agent's own machine at a moment: a file appears, a cache grows, a repository
goes stale. Minutehand runs the command then, in the folder the run was started from, with MINUTEHAND_NOW set
to the simulated moment (ISO 8601), so it can stamp what it makes; nobody is woken, as on a real machine.

Never stored

facts.description: What this person knows; all a model reply may draw on

reminded.description: What a follow-up does to an answer they owe; None: nothing, the answer lands when it was drawn

A person adds the agent to a conversation it is not in: invites its bot to a channel (Slack), or installs
its app in a team, a chat, or with no channel their own chat with it (Teams).

was due, from the run loop's table. Only a run Minutehand played keeps that table.

ProviderSeed.description:
What one provider seeds beyond the shared people, tickets and documents, in that provider's own shape.

The shared model cannot name a provider's types (`domain` imports no adapter), so the shape crosses as
the provider's own JSON text, as a stored entity's body does, and only that provider parses it: it
validates `body` against its own seed model when it seeds, and refuses what it cannot read. A scenario
file writes the shape as YAML or JSON structure; it is kept as its JSON text.

body.description: The provider's own seed model, as JSON text
body.title: Body

Rate.title: Rate

Reassigns.description: The person hands the ticket to someone else, or takes everyone off it.

Relayed.description:
The agent passed on what a person told it: a message from the agent to `to` holds every value of `holding`,
a fact the scenario's author gave `said_by` to say, matched in any case.

The values are facts, not the person's wording: a model writes the person's words, and the check reads whether
the fact reached `to`. A scenario is refused when its goal, a direction, a seeded ticket or document, or anyone
else's script or facts holds a value, and when `said_by` could never say it: silent, or none of their script's
steps or facts holds it. In a run, the agent's message must come after a reply of `said_by`'s that carries the
value (in its words, or in the facts its step was written from); an agent message that held it before means the
agent did not hear it from them, and no message counts.

to.description: Person.key the agent must pass it on to
to.title: To

Relayed.title: Relayed

Reminded.description:
What a follow-up does to an answer this person owes: a moment is drawn again from `sooner_within`, of their
available time after the follow-up, and the answer moves there when that is sooner. Never later.
Reminded.title: Reminded

written.description: Whose words, any of these; empty: any
written.title: Written

Scripted.description:
A plan of what this person knows, decides and does, step by step, in answer to the agent's messages. The
words are a model's, written from each step's facts in the person's voice, unless a step is `verbatim`.

A message whose number has no step, before the last step, gets no answer: the script says so. Once the steps
are used, the person keeps conversing (`then: answers`, the default), a model writing from their facts, until
the run ends; `then: silent` is the author's word that they say nothing more.

decisions.description: What they decide on items waiting on them in the agent's own product, after their delay like a reply. None says nothing: with `then: answers` a model decides every item, and with `then: silent` a run whose agent declares an inbox they can receive items in is refused. `[]` leaves every item to `then`

history_turns.description: How many messages of what they can see the model is shown word for word, the newest; older ones reach it as one summary, written by a model once and kept

model.description: None uses the run's default model
model.title: Model

voice.description: How they write: terse, formal, chatty

ScriptedDecision.description:
What this person decides on an item waiting on them in the agent's own product (`domain.inboxes`): the nth
such item (`to_item`), or every one (`to_item` None), in one inbox or in any. A decision naming its item wins
over one for every item. What they give with it (a reason, an answer) is written by a model from `facts`,
unless `inputs` fixes the words.

decision.description: The name of one of the inbox's decisions
decision.title: Decision

facts.description: Why they decide so, as facts the model writes each input from

inbox.description: The inbox's `name`; None: any. With one, `to_item` counts that inbox's items only

inputs.description: Each input the decision takes, by its name, in exact words: no model for those

to_item.description: The nth item waiting on them, from 1; None: every one

ScriptedPress.description:
Use a control on the message being answered instead of writing back: the one whose label reads `label`, as
the person sees it, in any case. When the agent answers the press by opening a form, the person fills it with
`form` and submits it.

ScriptedReply.description:
One step of a person's script: what they know, decide or do in answer to the nth message they receive.

By default the words are a model's, written from `facts` (what this reply carries) and `intent`, in the
person's voice; the step fixes what is said, never how. `verbatim` is the rare exact string, for a test that
needs those words and no others. `press` uses a control on the message instead of writing back.

verbatim.description: These exact words and no model: the rare opt-in

ToolCalled.description: The agent called this tool on an MCP server (`ToolCallSnapshot`), with these words in its arguments.

server.description: The server's host, or its relay's --name; None: any

Touches.description:
Every write of the agent's on the ask's person or its thread or ticket, open or not: after an answer, the
agent coming back to it. Read for `each: ask` or `handoff` only.
Touches.title: Touches

Transitions.description:
Transitions of items' states, by anyone (docs/design-transitions.md): each counted at the moment it was
made. States and names are the provider's own words, in any case.

by.description: Made by any of these; empty: by anyone
by.title: By

from.description: Out of any of these states; empty: out of any
from.title: From

name.description: Named any of these by the provider; empty: any
name.title: Name

not_reached.description: Its item had been in none of these states before it
not_reached.title: Not Reached

provider.description: In any of these providers; empty: in any
provider.title: Provider

reached.description: Its item had been in one of these states before it
reached.title: Reached

same_item.description: True: of the item of the transition the rule is read for (`each: transition`)
same_item.title: Same Item

to.description: Into any of these states; empty: into any
to.title: To

who.description: Made by any of these people; empty: by anyone or anything
who.title: Who

Transitions.title: Transitions

Trigger.description: Who moves an item along a transition, as a machine declares it; recorded as the `Actor` of the same name.
Trigger.title: Trigger

changed_world.description: False: the wake wrote nothing a person could see
changed_world.title: Changed World

When.description: A condition for reading the rule at all.

answered.description: It was answered, or the work finished, by the end
answered.title: Answered

open_at.description: The ask or hand-off was unanswered at this moment

stopped.description: The run stopped in one of these ways

Where.description:
Which of the things the rule is read for: by the person asked or handed the work, or who made the
transition; and, for `each: transition`, by its provider, name, states and who made it.

by.description: For `each: transition`: made by these only

name.description: For `each: transition`: named these by the provider only

provider.description: For `each: transition`: in these providers only

to.description: For `each: transition`: into these states only
to.title: To

Where.title: Where

Window.description:
When a person's answer lands: a moment drawn uniformly between `min` and `max` of the person's AVAILABLE
time after the ask, the time inside their working hours and outside their absences. Two hours of available
time asked at 16:00 on a Friday, of a person working 9 to 17 on weekdays, is 10:00 on Monday.
Window.title: Window

WorkingHours.description: Replies land only inside these hours, in this person's own timezone.
WorkingHours.title: WorkingHours

Writes.description: Every change the agent made to the world: what it created, updated or deleted.

gated.description: True: a call carrying an operation an item in the agent's own product held back (`gates`), made while that item was pending, turned down, or taken back undecided
gated.title: Gated

in_repeated_wake.description: True: written in a wake that was the second delivery of the same wake (`dispatch`)
in_repeated_wake.title: In Repeated Wake

operations.description: These operations; empty: any of the three
operations.title: Operations

repeats_open_ticket.description: True: a ticket created with the title (case, punctuation and spacing aside) of one still open in the same project

things.description: Of these kinds; empty: of any
things.title: Things

Written.description: Where a person's words came from (`domain.people.Writing`), as a rule names it.

description: A scenario as its file states it. With no `starts_at` it starts at the moment the run does.

assess.description: The team's rules for how the agent behaves in this scenario, over the facts of the run (`docs/assessments.md`); one with the id of an agent file's rule replaces it
assess.title: Assess

assess_off.description: Ids of the agent file's rules this scenario does not judge by
assess_off.title: Assess Off

channels.description: Conversations that exist when the run starts
channels.title: Channels

dispatch.description: Faults in delivering the agent's own wakes: late, twice or dropped. Without any, each is delivered at the moment it was asked for
dispatch.title: Dispatch

expect.description: What must be true of the world for this run to be right
expect.title: Expect

expect_outcome.description: The verdict this scenario is written to reach: every sample's, or, as a rate, the share of its samples that must (`{passed: ">= 0.9"}`); `minutehand run-all` exits 1 when it is missed
expect_outcome.title: Expect Outcome

fail_on_integrity.description: Integrity facts that fail the run, besides those the agent file names, when they are found (`around_proxy`, `agent_contract_changed`, `unmatched_call`); unnamed, each is stated as `review` and never changes the verdict
fail_on_integrity.title: Fail On Integrity

goal.description: The text handed to the agent, verbatim
goal.title: Goal

happenings.description: What people do by themselves, unprompted, at moments the scenario sets
happenings.title: Happenings

machine.description: What happens to the agent's own machine, at moments the scenario sets
machine.title: Machine

max_wakes.description: The most wakes a run plays before it stops; absent, sized from the deadline and the agent's rhythm (`domain.run.wake_limit`)
max_wakes.title: Max Wakes

memory.description: What the agent's memory (`minutehand.agent.store`) holds when the run starts: each key and its value. Nothing else is in it; the agent's own production database is never read
memory.title: Memory

owner.description: Person.key of whoever gave the goal
owner.title: Owner

protected_names.description: Names the agent must spell exactly as given
protected_names.title: Protected Names

provider_seeds.description: Each provider's own seed beyond people, tickets and documents; one per provider
provider_seeds.title: Provider Seeds

seed.description: Where every draw of the run comes from (each person's reply moments); None: one derived from the scenario's name. `minutehand run --seed` overrides it, and the run records the one it played
seed.title: Seed

services.description: Hosts no provider fakes that the agent files things with and people respond through: each item's state held and moved along a machine, what the agent is answered rendered from it (docs/services.md)
services.title: Services

starts_at.description: None: the moment the run starts
starts_at.title: Starts At

transitions_on.description: Providers whose people the people engine plays (docs/design-transitions.md): what waits on a person there is pending on them, and at their moment they take one of its legal transitions
